rules.title: Symbol prefix
rules.description: Top-level definitions start with a prefix of the package: its name or file name, its name without -mode or -themes, org- for an ox- package, or a parent package it requires; a with- or define- before the prefix is allowed.

sources.label: Emacs Lisp Reference Manual (Emacs 31.1): Emacs Lisp Coding Conventions
sources.quote: The names of all global symbols in your program, that is the names of variables, constants, and functions, should begin with that chosen prefix. Separate the prefix from the rest of the name with a hyphen, ‘-’.

sources.label: Emacs Lisp Reference Manual (Emacs 31.1): Emacs Lisp Coding Conventions
sources.quote: If one prefix is insufficient, your package can use two or three alternative common prefixes, so long as they make sense.

sources.label: Emacs Lisp Reference Manual (Emacs 31.1): Emacs Lisp Coding Conventions
sources.quote: constructs that define functions, variables, etc., may work better if they start with ‘define-’, so it’s okay to put the name prefix later on in the name.
